Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! Umpires are ready at their positions. The fielders have scattered. Stephan Pascal and Steve Wedderburn to open for West Indies Under-19. Charlie Anderson gets the duty to start with the new ball.
... THE RUN CHASE ...

On the other hand, this is the first time when the Aussie top order failed to make a good start. Both of their openers were dismissed in the first six overs of the Powerplay. The skipper, Hugh Weibgen and Sam Konstas were starting to build a partnership but it remained as a hallucination as the skipper had to walk down to the hut in the18th over. After this event the middle order shook up and they lost two of their middle order batters in quick succession. But Sam Konstas on the other end got a lucky as he was nicked a couple of times but kept knocking and rotating the strike. He made sure he cashed it well and he registered his half-century which was much needed for the Aussies. He partnered up with Rafael Macmillan and formed a strong partnership of 89 runs and anchored the innings till 43th over. But at the death, the collaboration broke down with the dismissal of Rafael Macmillan but Sam Konstas was not stopping to go big on the loose deliveries. Yet again, the trails of wickets were falling on one end but Konstas stayed calm and scored a brilliant 108 off 121 deliveries and made sure to stretch the score line as much as possible so that the bowlers had enough confidence to defend it. A really exciting chase is coming up with a lot on the line. Join us in a bit for the second essay.

Isai Thorne is up for a quick chat. He says that they started well but the Aussies came back well despite bowling tight and neat. He continues that he has performed well in these last couple of matches as he is executing the plans well and gaining a lot of experience as well. He ends up saying that the batting unit will also try to keep things simple and a couple of partnerships should help them chase this down smoothly.

West Indies Under-19 will be happy with their bowling effort, but would have been happier if they managed to restrict the Aussies under 200 here. Their opening pace duo started magnificently as they slayed both of the openers in two consecutive overs at the initial stage of the inning. Credit goes to Stephan Pascal for his aggressive field settings that put pressure on the batters and ultimately got the rewards. One way or the other it helped the Windies to dismiss Hugh Weibgen, the in-form batter of their opposition. That created even more pressure and resulted in another wicket for them. They had the opponents at 87/5, but let them build up a stand as the standard of fielding went down as the game went on. A big partnership between Sam Konstas and Rafael Macmillan created loads of problems for them. However, the skipper Stephan Pascal stepped up by taking a screamer and breaking the partnership which eased the situation a little bit. At the end of the innings, Nathan Edward finished with three wickets, while Isai Thorne got a couple.  Whereas, Raneico Smith, Nathan Sealy, and Tarrique Edward chipped in for one each. The bowling unit has done its job but now all eyes are on the batting unit to chase down the score if they want to keep their semi-final hopes alive.

A brilliant hundred from Sam Konstas has helped Australia Under-19 to a respectable total! They fought back really well here and showed why the Aussies have the best temperament to get out of pressure situations.

A couple of runs to end the innings then! Nathan Edward bangs this short and on middle, Harkirat Bajwa backs away and swats it wide of long on and comes back for the second run. Australia Under-19 finish on 227/8!

The Super Six phase of this ICC Under-19 Cricket World Cup has given us some nail-biting clashes to witness and the action continues with Match 8 where West Indies Under-19 will fight against Australia Under-19 at Diamond Oval, Kimberley. Both teams are on the winning momentum and both of these cricketing giants carry some luck up their sleeves as well. West Indies Under-19 got under the cosh in the game against Sri Lanka Under-19 as they dramatically collapsed in the last ten overs of the run chase. The skipper Stephan Pascal with his 33 and his opening partner Steve Wedderburn's immaculate 67 provided a fantastic start along with Jordan Johnson's 39. Still, West Indies' middle order tumbled a bit against the Lankan spin web. But Nathan Sealy and Tarrique Edward eventually sailed them through the winning line, negotiating the spin maturely, with just three balls remaining. Raneico Smith shined with his excellent 4-fer and the others picked one scalp a piece. They currently stand in the third position on the Points Table in Group 2 of the Super Six. Coming to one of the dominating teams of this competition, the anticipation was too high for the mini Ashes but, Australia Under-19 too, had some fortunes favouring them as rain played some role in their win, but overall, it was their all-round dominance which eventually held them to the win. They posted 266 on the board and were helped by their skipper Hugh Weibgen's scintillating 120 along with Harry Dixon's 53. Their middle order too, contributed some valuable runs. Coming to defend their score against England Under-19, rain played the spoilsport and the match was reduced to 24 overs and the DLS target was 215. With the situation favouring the Aussies after the rain, they didn't let any English batters settle and tightened the screws. Callum Vidler was the pick of the bowlers with his excellent 4-fer and he was complimented well by his bowling mates Rafael Macmillan and Tom Straker who picked three and two wickets respectively. They bundled out England Under-19 on a mere score of 104 and won the mini Ashes by 114 runs, stepping one more step ahead in the journey to the semis and currently top Group 2 of the Super Six. Australia Under-19 hold a fantastic winning streak at this venue, winning all four matches they have played here, and that too, with considerable margins. But, West Indies Under-19 are no less than fighters. Well, they can take the motivation from their seniors who narrowly defeated Australia in the Brisbane Test on their home soil and injected the fighting spirit among the young guns. This exciting clash promises to provide some nail-biting moments as well. Whom are you supporting?
